name: Jonathan Gannon

views.text: A team should be adaptable, physical, explosive and smart, and every plan should show all four.
Stay where your feet are; this week's work is the only one you can win.
Put defenses in conflict: when a run and a pass look the same, they have to guess.
A dynamic quarterback is a problem for every defense, and the offense should lean into that.
Hire coaches for how they think and whether they serve players, not for their age.
Loving football means you never have to look for motivation.
When the head coach loses his composure, he owns it in front of the team, apologizes and moves on.

signatures: leans on a stock of short catchphrases that reporters start collecting
brings players into the room at big announcements and speaks to them directly
apologizes to the team as a group when he crosses a line
want: to build Arizona into a physical, adaptable winner around a young staff he hand-picked
fear: that the heat that makes him energizing on the sideline turns into a moment that defines him
voice: High-energy, emphatic and full of slogans; he speaks in punchy phrases and repeats a few favorite expressions. He talks up toughness, adaptability and staying present, and is effusive about players he likes. When he gets something wrong he names it plainly and apologizes.

evidence.summary: Introduced four days after his Eagles lost the Super Bowl, he stresses staying in the present, praises Murray as a rare problem for defenses, and says he never needs to look for motivation because he loves football. Writer contrasts his energy with the reserved previous coach.

Speaking to players seated up front, he lays out a team built on adaptability, physicality, explosiveness and smarts; GM Ossenfort says his energy never dropped in interviews and Ertz, who played for him in Philadelphia, calls him a great leader who stayed in touch. Team site.

A light guide to seven recurring phrases from his introduction about accountability, team-first play, bold action and focus; Bidwill says he used one favorite word in about a dozen ways in his interview. Shows a speaking habit, not substance.

He hires Petzing, 35, who worked with him in Minnesota, and Rallis, 29, his Eagles linebackers coach and a Vikings colleague, saying age was never a factor and he judged candidates on thinking and character. Team site.
Gannon says he fully trusts Rallis to run the defense, cares more about serving players and results than age, and asks candidates about the best and worst things their bosses did. Team site.

Explains Murray taking more snaps under center in 2023; Gannon says the aim was to create conflict so defenses cannot tell run from pass, and Petzing stresses that every look must appear identical. Scheme detail with quotes.

The team fines him $100,000 after video shows him shouting at and swiping toward running back Demercado following a costly fumble; he says he apologized to the player and team, let the moment overwhelm him, and calls it a mistake. One incident; the league took no action.
